notes.text: Note.— This roll was sent with the others of the same command and was marked Company A. This was evidently a mistake, as that company was given in another roll which corresponds with the record in the Roll of Honor. The companies of this regiment were designated in a curious way and so reversed all military rules that I supposed this must have been the missing roll of Com- pany C, and so have inserted it. It will be observed that it is a very imperfect record, and does not even give the name of the Captain.

Not only half the men who went out with Capt. Rellly in 1801, bnt the remainder of the regiment were only to be found In the Archives Office in Washington. The reader will observe how miserably ex- 'ecuted were even these report^s originally sent to Richmond, but captured in 1K63, and traMsferred to the Federal Capital. notes.text: Note.— No story was ever more marred in the telling than the record of this reglmo?»t- I couW find In Nortli Carolina nothing but the roll of Battery A, in the "Roll of Honor" and the few names reported in Rumple's "History of Rowan," as belonging to Battery D. Not only half the men who went out with Capt. Rellly in 1801, bnt the remainder of the regiment were only to be found In the Archives Office in Washington. The reader will observe how miserably ex- 'ecuted were even these report^s originally sent to Richmond, but captured in 1K63, and traMsferred to the Federal Capital. Not only were the casnaltles, but <jven the residences of the men omitted, and in this way there may bearrors as to some of the homes attributed.
